meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (bijural: civil law for Quebec private/commercial law; common law for federal and public law)

Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 83.01 et seq. (terrorism financing); United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 13; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (articles 26-37 regarding ultimate beneficiaries); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and attestation of registration from Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by Global Affairs Canada (Canada party to the 1961 Apostille Convention with effect from 11 January 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized true copies of government-issued photo identity documents for each director, officer and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in country of origin or Canadian embassy/consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is party; otherwise consular legalization by the Embassy of Canada or local competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration / declaration of ultimate beneficial owner (declaration du beneficiaire ultime)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary or commissioner for oaths in the state of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as required by counterparty bank or regulator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for representation before REQ, CRA and Revenu Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in Quebec or in the foreign signatory's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; Quebec notarial deed may be used without apostille within Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory client identification and verification under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidelines: (1) verify the identity of every director, officer, shareholder and UBO using valid government-issued photo identification; (2) identify and verify all persons directly or indirectly owning, controlling or directing 25% or more of the corporation; (3) screen all directors, UBOs and authorized signatories against Canadian sanctions lists under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada autonomous sanctions, OFAC SDN List for any USD payment rail or US correspondent banking, and PEP databases (e.g., World-Check/Refinitiv); (4) apply enhanced due diligence for any senior foreign political figure, head of state, or family member/close associate under FINTRAC PEHIO rules; (5) conduct ongoing transaction monitoring and file suspicious transaction reports with FINTRAC; (6) document all screening and beneficial ownership findings in an AML/CFT compliance file maintained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec / Quebec Enterprise Register (REQ) online services: https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptor, and a permitted legal element (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Societe par actions'). Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the registered legal name must be in a French form unless the exception applies for a natural person's name or recognized trademark; transliteration into Latin script with French accent conventions is applied by the REQ. A non-French operating name may be used commercially only if the French registered name is present on signage, invoices and business documents with at least equal prominence.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On refusal of a name reservation, REQ issues a motivated refusal notice. The applicant may file a written 'demande de revision' with REQ within 30 days from the notice, setting out legal grounds for compliance and paying the prescribed fee; REQ must issue a decision within 15 working days. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant may apply to the Superior Court of Quebec (Cour superieure) for judicial review within 60 days of the revised decision. A name reservation cannot be extended; after the 60-day validity window, the applicant must submit a new name search request and pay a new fee. In urgent cases, a request for expedited review may be made to REQ.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for registered office and service of process only where the service provider maintains a physical street address in Quebec and forwards mail; it does not satisfy REQ establishment requirements or Canadian tax residence indicators, and it is not sufficient for a dental clear aligner manufacturer. A physical production, storage or quality-control facility in Quebec and a Health Canada medical device establishment licence are expected for commercial substance and regulatory compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 40% (moderate): Revenu Quebec and Health Canada may perform unannounced on-site inspections of medical device establishments, and REQ/Revenu Quebec may verify registered office addresses and commercial substance indicators during the first 24 months after incorporation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Québec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 19, 42-43, 126; Legal Publicity Act, CQLR c P-44.1; Regulation respecting the Annual Declaration of Registraire des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar); online system at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution) filed electronically with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, followed by registration in the Quebec Enterprise Register and issuance of an attestation of legal existence
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Québec Business Corporation; shares may be issued without nominal or par value and no escrow account is required. Where consideration is non-cash, directors must fix fair value in accordance with ss. 38-39 QBCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the shares subscribed by each incorporator be and are hereby issued, allotted, and entered in the securities register of the Corporation as fully paid, and that the consideration fixed by the board be accepted and recorded. RESOLVED: That the registered head office of the Corporation be fixed at [street address], [city], Québec, and that the directors execute and file all declarations, notices, and prescribed forms with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec as required by law. RESOLVED: That ________ be and is hereby appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, ________ Treasurer, and ________ Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED: That the proposed standard by-laws, banking resolutions, and corporate records be and are hereby adopted and ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Reservation, and NUANS Pre-validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Quebec Enterprise Register online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search on the REQ database; where requested, obtain a Quebec NUANS-style name report and reservation valid for 90 days, or elect to incorporate using the Numbered Company option. File the name reservation request online, pay the fee, and obtain a confirmation number to be quoted in the articles of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed name search request (Form DAI-a or online equivalent)
Fee payment receipt for name reservation
Proof of signatory authority and identity (government-issued ID, juridical extract if incorporated parent)
Memorandum of name acceptability where the name contains a distinctive element or protected term
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, file an amended name reservation with revised wording within the statutory response period, or appeal the refusal to the REQ with a written legal rationale; alternatively, incorporate under a registered number and later file articles of amendment for a name change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Constitution en ligne (online incorporation service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of incorporation setting out the corporation name or number, registered office address, share classes and rights, restrictions on transfer, number of directors (or minimum/maximum), and any business restrictions. Submit the articles electronically via the REQ 'constitution en ligne' module; authorize the payment; receive a signed attestation of existence and the enterprise registration number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation under Part IA QBCA
Name reservation confirmation or numerical designation
Filing fee payment (approx. CAD 377)
Electronic declaration appointing first directors, where not included in the articles
Consent of first directors to act (Form, if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a query or correction notice, respond within 30 days by amending the articles or submitting an explanatory covering schedule; where the application is rejected as incomplete, resubmit with the exact corrections and pay the applicable processing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Documentation, Share Subscription, and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate records office (directors' minutes) with subsequent attestation to REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board of directors meeting; adopt the pro-forma resolution, authorize issuance of shares to incorporators, fix the head office address, appoint officers, approve the standard by-laws, set the fiscal year end, and retain a corporate securities register and minutes book. File the required 'decisions' declarations and any prescribed forms with REQ if the by-laws amend the articles' director provisions.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes
Subscriptions list and share certificate stubs
Consent of officers and directors
By-law No. 1 (general operating by-law)
Registered office notice and information sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ministerial defect notices are cured through unanimous written resolutions or retroactive council resolutions; any inconsistency between board actions and REQ declarations is remedied by filing an amending declaration and paying the late-filing penalty if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Revenu Québec, QST/GST Accounts, and CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Quebec Revenue Agency) and CNESST (Workers' Compensation Board)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the new corporation with Revenu Québec using the NEQ; obtain the Quebec Business Number (QN), register for GST/HST and QST together with payroll source deductions (e.g., the NQ account), and establish the CNESST dossier with the industrial classification code for manufacturing that corresponds to NAICS 339114. Complete the online file information sections strictly within 30 days post-incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (attestation de constitution)
Enterprise registration certificate (NEQ extract)
Directors' consent forms
Completed Revenu Québec Enterprise Registration Form LM-1
CNESST insurance registration declaration
Lease and proof of commercial address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec requests more evidence or objects to the classification, file an administrative review request within 90 days; for CNESST misclassification, submit the employment classification review request under the Act respecting industrial accidents and occupational diseases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Publicity and Annual Statutory Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the initial annual declaration is filed with REQ no later than 60 days after incorporation and thereafter annually within the prescribed deadline; publish the identities of directors, the head office, and any registration changes; maintain legal publicity by filing updates within 15-30 days of any change to directors or the registered office.
required_dossiers: Annual enterprise register declaration
List of directors and the date of termination for any director removed
Notice of change of head office or directors where applicable
Revenu Québec business number and QST registration
Updated securities register from minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is rejected retroactively, immediately file the corrected declaration with the REQ and pay the late-filing penalty; administrative revocation of the juridical person's registration can be cured by filing a 'request for reinstatement' accompanied by all outstanding returns and confirmation evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada, Medical Devices Bureau; Ministère de la Santé et des Services sociaux du Québec
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Food and Drugs Act and the Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282), required for class II clear-aligner thermoformed sheets manufactured, packaged, and distributed in Canada; ISO 13485:2016 certification (recommended commercial baseline for healthcare market access)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III 'Registration' (déclaration de conformité) under Chapter IV.1 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) for a thermoforming and trimming facility without significant air or water loading; a full environmental impact assessment is not ordinarily required where the process is limited to heat-forming polymer sheets, CNC trimming, washing, and sterile-adjacent packaging. If the installation includes solvent-based adhesives or plastic surface coating above a de minimis threshold, a ministerial authorization in accordance with Chapter IV.1 may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal sewers must meet the municipal pre-treatment by-laws and provincial standards (pH 6.0-9.5; total suspended solids and organic loading within limits set in the municipal sewer by-law); VOC and particulate emissions are subject to the Clean Air Regulation (Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère, CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1) and federal Canadian Environmental Protection Act; process wastes, scrap polymer and detergent-contaminated packaging must be characterized and disposed in compliance with the Hazardous Materials Regulation (Règlement sur les matières dangereuses, R.R.Q. c. Q-2, r. 32).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and annual inspection by the competent municipal fire prevention service (Régime d'implantation); building permit and certificate of occupancy issued by the municipal building inspection department in application of the Québec Building Act and Construction Code; workforce access and occupational safety clearance through the CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1), including a mandatory prevention program, electrical hazard inspection of thermoforming lines, machine guarding certificates, and a documented evacuation and contamination control plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and federal corporate income tax; Revenu Québec for the Québec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) and Quebec provincial corporate income tax; Portals: CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec Clic Revenu / Mon Dossier d'Entreprise
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation not resident in Canada must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and a non-resident GST/HST account via CRA (Form RC391 or RC1, granting a 9-digit BN with an RT prefix). For Quebec nexus, the entity must obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) by registering extra-provincially with the Registraire d'entreprises (REQ) (Form AR-1/AR-1A), then register with Revenu Québec for the QST using the QST registration form attached to the NEQ (QST registrant number sequenced as NR prefix or TQ preceded by the NEQ). Registration is mandatory within 30 days of exceeding the small-supplier threshold or engaging in a taxable activity requiring a permit/licence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian federal/provincial business corporation is a separate taxable legal person subject to Part I federal corporate income tax and Quebec Part IV corporate income tax; no pass-through or transparent treatment is available for corporate shareholders, and worldwide income of a resident corporation is subject to Canadian taxation with foreign tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box classification regime; corporate status is determined by the incorporating statutes. Relevant statutory elections include: GST/HST closely related corporation election (Section 156, Excise Tax Act), Quick Method of accounting election for GST/HST and QST, Section 216 election for non-resident rental income, and Section 219 corporate branch returns election; hybrid mismatch rules adopted under BEPS Action 2 (2021-2023) deny deduction/non-inclusion benefits but do not create entity classification choices.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Good and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus QST (Québec Sales Tax) — Quebec administers its own VAT-compliant QST system collected alongside the GST; dental aligner sheets are taxable supplies subject to GST and QST in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made during any single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold) for both GST/HST and QST; a non-resident is also required to register if its worldwide taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000 and supplies are made in Canada, subject to the same small-supplier exceptions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping regime currently applies in Canada or Quebec; the CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices if the EDI/electronic format contains all prescribed information and supports complete audit trails. Quebec's Act respecting the modernization of invoicing provisions will make standardized electronic invoicing (B2B and B2C) and electronic reporting to Revenu Québec mandatory on a phased schedule: from September 2026 for enterprises with annual turnover above C$15 million and from September 2027 for all other taxable suppliers; the regime mandates structured-format issuance and transmission via the Boomerang/ government-recognized components rather than a single-state fiscal clearance API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada by a registrant to a non-resident recipient, including dental clear aligner sheets shipped from Quebec to foreign orthodontic laboratories, provided (i) title and possession of the goods transfer to the non-resident before or at export, (ii) the goods are exported as soon after the supply as is reasonable and in accordance to the supplier's normal business practice, and (iii) the supplier maintains evidence of export (e.g., bills of lading, customs B13A declarations, shipping contracts). Offshore services rendered to non-residents may also qualify for zero-rating if not part of a Canadian business undertaking; QST zero-rating mirrors the GST/HST Schedule VI rules for exporting goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A or approved electronic export declaration) endorsed at the port of export
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Canada to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank account statement proving receipt of foreign-currency payment from the non-resident customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess and claw back zero-rated treatment where export documentation or actual export is deficient, with reassessment periods extending 4 years generally and up to 10 years in cases of misrepresentation at any time; penalties for false statements or willful participation in a false claim under the Excise Tax Act reach the greater of 20% of the net tax owed and CAD 500 plus interest, with gross negligence penalties of up to 50% of the refund and criminal exposure including fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment where deliberate evasion is established; QST equivalents apply under the Québec Tax Administration Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange policy is administered by the Department of Finance Canada, with transaction-level monitoring and reporting enforcement under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) through the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible and freely floating currency regime for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls, prior authorizations, or surrender requirements. Capital injection, dividend remittance, management fees, and intercompany loan repayments are subject to normal corporate law solvency tests and Quebec Civil Code restrictions on unlawful dividends, and to non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Part XIII) and applicable treaty provisions. Profit remittance is structurally free but may be subject to a 25% domestic withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, reduced to 5% or 15% under the Canada-US treaty, and to anti-money laundering beneficial ownership disclosure. Medical/dental aligner revenues from export sales are freely convertible into CAD or any other currency; no forced conversion or X-code licensing applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to deposit export receipts in a designated domestic account. Exporters may contract, invoice, and hold proceeds in any convertible currency. However, for receipts of CAD 10,000 or more in a single direction, financial institutions and the reporting entity must complete an Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) report to FINTRAC; the underlying commercial invoice, bill of lading, and customs export documentation (via the Canadian Border Services Agency, or under the U.S.-Canada periodic reporting mechanism) must be retained for the six-year record-keeping period set out in the PCMLTFA Regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with significant legal constraints. A purely offshore digital EMI (e.g., a UK FCA-authorised e-money institution) may not directly maintain a Canadian-dollar operating account or provide cross-border payments for a Quebec entity unless it is registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA and, if operating in Quebec, holds a valid licence under the Quebec Money-Services Businesses Act (chapter S-6.01) or partners with a chartered bank. An unregistered offshore EMI is legally prohibited from providing its services to persons resident in Canada and can trigger both FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties and an inability to establish clearing through the Canadian Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS). As a practical matter, using an EMI as the primary treasury rail is not advisable for a Quebec-domiciled aligner producer; the robust route is a domestically incorporated credit union, Schedule I bank, or a Quebec trust company that offers API-based banking and correspondent USD/CAD clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors may be required to complete an in-person or video-verified identity interview before the onboarding is approved. In Quebec, the Business Corporations Act (Québec) and a bank's internal corporate onboarding policy typically demand that the subscribing director(s) and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) with 25% or more control provide original government-issued photo identification, a notarized corporate by-law, and Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) confirmation. While the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and FINTRAC permit a risk-based remote identity verification solution (including video capture and electronic verification), in practice at least one of the authorized signatories will be prompted to attend a branch in Quebec or a notary public to execute the borrowing resolution and the account signing authority. Full remote opening without a physical presence is available only if the corporation is onboarded through an approved fintech link (e.g., RBC's digital onboarding or National Bank's BanqueEn Ligne for business), subject to a laxer AML procedure and a credit-check limitation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenues from an exported medical/dental product are being intermingled with professional orthodontic services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete corporate file: ISO 13485 quality-management certificate (for aligner manufacturing/thermoforming), Health Canada medical-device establishment licence (SNDS/SWL if required), the NAICS 339114 classification certificate, the signed master supply agreement for clear-aligner sheets, product HS codes, a lineage of quarterly audited purchase orders, and a representation letter distinguishing product sales from non-regulated dental-agent services, together with a Quebec business number and TP-1 corporate registration confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder structure with no Canadian family nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified corporate registry extract (from Registraire des entreprises), a complete Organizational Chart of ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) with proof of identity and proof of residential address for each 25%+ owner, a PSC register under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if federal) or the Quebec Business Corporations Act, a non-solicitation/non-tax-haven declaration, tax residency certificates from the beneficial owners' jurisdictions, and a business-plan narrative explaining the direct investment by the offshore shareholder, including the source-of-wealth documentation and professional references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of platform payment rails (Stripe/credit-card) with unusually high transaction volume for dental aligners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the completed merchant underwriting file: platform pay-out schedule, chargeback-history letter, refund policy, 24-month financial projections, revenue ledger of subscription/orthodontist billing, the platform's KYC/KYB reports, and a PCI-DSS compliance attestation. Additionally, file with the bank a letter from the controller confirming that the platform-based receivables will be swept daily to the chartered bank account and are not used as inventory substitutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large intercompany shareholders-loan contribution routed from a foreign parent into a fresh Alberta/Quebec subsidiary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare an intercompany loan agreement (no usury concern), a board resolution authorizing the incurrence of indebtedness, provincial registry proof of the borrowing by-law, the parent's audited financial statements showing available liquidity, and evidence of the funding source (e.g., CBI circular letter for the parent's own bank). If the contribution is a non-resident investment, attach the completed Form RC431 to FINTRAC and, when necessary, file a report of the transaction under section 7 of the Investment Canada Act (for review thresholds).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound investment capital is best wired by SWIFT MT103 from a bank of the parent/holding company to the Quebec corporation's CAD-denominated account at a Schedule I bank. The wire must carry a remittance information field identifying the sender, the beneficiary as CA_CORP, and a clear purpose code such as 'Equity injection for subsidiary / shareholder loan — direct investment in Canada'. The receiving Canadian financial institution will perform a source-of-funds and purpose-of-payment analysis in line with PCMLTFA; the company should proactively provide the corporate resolution, the shareholder loan note, and the Registraire des entreprises certificate to avoid a regulatory hold. Cross-border wire values in excess of CAD 10,000 trigger the FINTRAC EFT report from the bank, and the corporation must keep a corresponding compliance file. No currency conversion approval is needed, but if the inbound wire is denominated in a non-CAD currency, the bank will use its own mark or a spot transaction to credit the account in CAD, with an FX confirmation document created for the corporate treasury records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For clearance of inventory/sheet materials from external suppliers and sales settlements, the company will use: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers for trade invoices, especially for USD/CAD commercial payments to Korean/European sheet producers, (2) commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600 by a Quebec branch, advised through beneficiary banks, for bulk multi-layer aligner sheet purchases, and (3) domestic clearing via the Canadian ACSS and interbank Large-Value Transfer System (LVTS) for CAD-denominated supplier disbursements. Manual clearing operations must be accompanied by an export/import invoice, bill of lading, and customs entry to satisfy both the PCMLTFA record-retention and the Canada Revenue Agency excise/duty compliance; the banking channel will automatically report all cross-border transfers that exceed CAD 10,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD) with a Canadian Schedule I bank or registered OTC derivatives dealer
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD) where the entity trades fixed or floating cash flows on a notional principal
Zero-cost collars and three-way collars on USD/CAD for receipt-side hedging of export proceeds
Window forwards and average-rate forwards (average forward contracts) for periodic disbursement and receivable hedging
Currency options (puts and calls on USD/CAD) when paired with a commercial loan or trade financing facility

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for illiquid emerging-market currencies not reflecting actual underlying exposure; NDFs for USD/CAD are unnecessary and generally not individually permissible as speculative instruments, because CAD is fully deliverable and freely convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (CBCA) filed online with Corporations Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Two consecutive overdue annual returns may trigger a notice of intention to dissolve; failure to remedy after notice results in administrative strike-off and dissolution of the corporation under the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of the enterprise registration date, or by the date stated in the REQ reminder notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative deletion from the Quebec enterprise register; the corporation is then dissolved and loses legal capacity until reinstatement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal corporate income tax filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; any applicable income tax balance is due two or three months after year-end depending on Canadian-controlled private corporation status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; daily interest is compounded on arrears and the CRA may assess directors' liability if taxes are collectible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CO-17 Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (provincial corporate income tax filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end, aligned with the federal T2 filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of 5% of the unpaid provincial tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; interest is compounded daily and enforced collection measures may be taken.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Audit and Minute Book Maintenance (internal corporate records review)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records kept at the Quebec registered office; available to shareholders, directors, and regulators; not ordinarily filed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per fiscal year before the annual meeting or written resolution; registers must be current when the annual declaration is submitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or incomplete registers are offences under the CBCA and QBCA; directors may be fined on summary conviction, and inaccurate records expose the corporation to regulator inquiries.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Canadian corporate law does not impose revenue or asset thresholds for the federal or Quebec private business corporation. A mandatory independent audit applies to reporting issuers and to corporations whose shareholders do not validly waive the auditor appointment. A private corporation may dispense with an auditor for each fiscal year by a shareholder consent or resolution, provided no CBCA or QBCA rule requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for public/reporting issuers; Canadian private enterprises may use IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook. Quebec private corporations commonly apply ASPE unless the shareholders or creditors require IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CBCA requires every corporation to maintain an internal register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) at the registered office; this register is not filed with Corporations Canada but must be updated within 15 days after the corporation learns of a change. On any share transfer, the Register of Members and the ISC register must be updated before the transfer is treated as effective. The annual board review should formally confirm that the ISC register, register of members, and director registers are accurate. In Quebec, the annual declaration to the REQ must accurately reflect the corporation's directors, officers, and other registered information; material changes must be transmitted promptly to the Registraire.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 150–CAD 400 (approx. USD 110–300) per year for a Quebec registered office or registered agent; the cost is lower or nil if the corporation uses its own Quebec premises as its registered office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 3,000–CAD 10,000 (approx. USD 2,200–7,400) for a simple private manufacturing or sales corporation; reduced or nil where a valid unanimous shareholder waiver of auditor appointment is in effect

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (Federal 15.0% plus Quebec 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: combined effective rate of approximately 12.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (Federal 9.0% plus Quebec 3.2%); Quebec integrated manufacturing/production tax credits; Federal SR&ED investment tax credits; Quebec innovation and interactive digital media credits where applicable to aligner production software or manufacturing processes

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), administered via T2 e-File or certified tax preparation software through CRA My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; tax payable is due in full 2 months after the fiscal year-end, except 3 months for qualifying CCPCs within the small business limit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, Business Number (BN), account identifiers, fiscal period start and end dates, province/territory of registration, industry code (NAICS 339114), and registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must identify their Canadian permanent establishment and residency treaty position; enter the foreign jurisdiction code and attach treaty-residence certificate details

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All income from sales of thermoformed dental clear aligner sheets, other business revenues and investment income less deductible expenses, capital cost allowance, and allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report only Canadian-source taxable income attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment, applying functional and factual allocation of costs and revenues to the manufacturing and distribution functions performed in Canada

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income minus exempt amounts, prior-year non-capital loss carryovers, charitable donations, and other specified deductions allocable to the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct expenses reasonably connected to the Canadian PE under section 115 of the Income Tax Act; deductions are denied where expenses relate to foreign-source income not attributable to the PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes federal basic tax at 15% of taxable income for general corporations; CCRs use the 9% small business rate on Tier 1 taxable income and add provincial abatement adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 9% small business rate is unavailable to non-resident-owned corporations except in limited treaty-defined CCPC ownership structures; general 15% rate applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tracks eligible retained earnings taxed at the general rate; the balance determines whether future dividend distributions are eligible dividends for treaty withholding purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should receive a dividend classification statement; eligible dividends may qualify for reduced withholding treaty rates in the source jurisdiction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal corporate income tax payable after credits, tax credits, and installment payments; balance due is remitted to the CRA with the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must remit the balance due through CRA My Business Account and align payment with the 2-month or 3-month deadline, otherwise daily arrears interest commences

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% for each full month, up to 12 months; a further penalty of up to 10% is added where a demand to file is ignored; fixed statutory penalty of CAD 100 may also apply; repeat failure attracts extra penalties and CRA may apply public disclosure under the Taxpayer Relief provisions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return — Revenu Québec, filed electronically through Revenu Québec Online Corporate Services or certified electronic filing software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; Quebec balance due is 3 months after fiscal year-end for CCPCs qualifying for the small business rate, otherwise 2 months after fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), QST account number, legal name, head office address, fiscal period start and end, and legal form
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Quebec permanent establishment must disclose the PE address and attach any intercompany transaction schedules to enable provincial transfer pricing review

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues including sales of aligner sheets, conversion services, and any intra-group sales invoiced from the Quebec entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent revenues are excluded unless attributable to a Quebec PE; Quebec allocation uses a two-factor formula based on sales and wages attributable to the Quebec establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after incorporating federal taxable income, Quebec additions, and Quebec deductions such as loss carryovers and the Quebec exemption for foreign affiliates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents claim only income and expenses associated with the Quebec PE; no deduction is available for costs incurred by a foreign head office without a clear Canadian business nexus

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applies the Quebec 11.5% general rate or the 3.2% small business rate on eligible active business income of CCPCs with a Quebec permanent establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The small business rate is denied where a non-resident controls the corporation, unless the business income qualifies under treaty business-profits provisions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Refundable and non-refundable Quebec credits, including manufacturing investment credits, R&D innovation credits, and credits for qualifying computerized design used in aligner production
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refundable credits are generally denied to non-residents unless the credit amount is attributable to a Quebec PE; carryback and transfer rules differ by credit

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance due plus 1% per month, up to 12 months; minimum penalty applies for non-filing; additional penalties and compounded interest apply from the statutory due date

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, reduced by applicable tax treaty; Canada-US treaty: 15% general, 5% for qualifying corporate beneficial owners holding at least 10% voting power; Canada-China treaty: 15% general, 10% for directly held shareholdings of at least 10% capital
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief at source: the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain an official Certificate of Residence from the home jurisdiction tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for US residents) and deliver it to the Canadian payer together with a completed CRA non-residency declaration; the payer may then reduce the withholding before remittance to the CRA; where withholding was fully imposed, the non-resident files Form NR7-R with the CRA within two years from the end of the calendar year to obtain a refund; Revenu Québec generally follows the CRA treaty claims and accepts the same certificate filing for Quebec Part-IV-equivalent withholdings
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties to non-residents: statutory Part XIII rate 25%, treaty-reduced to 10% under both Canada-US and Canada-China treaties; interest paid at arm's length to non-residents is exempt from Part XIII tax; interest to specified shareholders is statutorily 25%, reduced to 0% under the Canada-US treaty for arm's length interest, 15% for excess interest, and to 10% under the Canada-China treaty

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000: annually aggregated related-party transactions of this size or greater are expected to be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation acceptable to the CRA under IC87-2R; Country-by-Country Reporting (CbC) applies where consolidated group revenue exceeds CAD 750,000,000, requiring a Master File and Local File structure consistent with OECD guidance
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) statute comparable to zero-tax jurisdictions; economic substance is nevertheless enforced through the corporate residency test of central management and control, the general anti-avoidance rule (subsection 245(2) of the Income Tax Act), Quebec's artificial-transaction rule under the Taxation Act, treaty limitation-on-benefits provisions, and the Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation (EIFEL) effective for taxation years beginning on or after October 1, 2023, which denies interest deductions where the group does not evidence sufficient taxable presence and financing substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly making false or misleading statements in the T2 or CO-17 returns, falsifying books and records, deliberately omitting Canadian product sales, inflating deductible expenses, or colluding with returns preparers to understate taxable income from dental aligner sheet manufacturing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under subsection 239(1) of the Income Tax Act: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment of up to 2 years on summary conviction or up to 5 years on indictment; civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% under subsection 163.2; Quebec parallel fines and seizures under the Tax Administration Act; automatic reassessment and compound accruing interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and accountants are personally prosecuteable; the corporate veil is lifted on evidence of personal direction or fraud; courts may impose restitution, disgorgement of tax savings, asset freezing, travel bans, and extradition or Interpol red notices for cross-border profit concealment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Payroll Source Deductions and GST/QST
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to deduct and remit employee income tax, CPP, EI, Quebec QPIP premiums, and failing to remit GST/HST and Quebec QST collected on aligner product sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The corporation is liable for 100% of unremitted amounts plus accrued interest; additional penalties apply of 10% of the unpaid source-deduction amount and 10% for QST discrepancies; CRA and Revenu Québec may seize bank accounts, garnish receivables, and register judgments against corporate assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors incur joint and several personal liability under subsection 227.1 of the Income Tax Act and section 323 of the Excise Tax Act for all unremitted source deductions and GST/QST regardless of corporate solvency; the due-diligence defense is strictly construed and requires proactive supervision; personal travel bans, asset seizures, and denial of export clearances are available enforcement measures

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Arrangement / Shell Corporation / Artificial Transaction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a non-resident holding structure with no economic substance to control Canadian IP and interpose artificial mark-ups on intercompany sales of clear aligner materials, while the Quebec corporation operates with minimal employees, no independent board decisions, and no real distribution functions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may apply the sham doctrine to recharacterize the arrangement, disregard intercompany agreements, deny expense deductions, reassess profits to the Canadian entity, impose transfer pricing penalties of 10%, and apply the general anti-avoidance rule to disallow the full tax benefit; Quebec reassessment may be adjusted under anti-artificial transaction provisions; treaty benefits may be denied on appeal
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute sham transactions face personal tax liability for unpaid corporate taxes through section 160 transfer provisions, which reassess against the beneficiary; the corporate veil is pierced where the shell is a conduit; civil restitution orders, director travel restrictions, and criminal liability for conspiracy to defraud the revenue authority are enforceable against directing minds

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Deficiencies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for dental aligner sheets, royalties, management fees, or financing that deviate from arm's length results, failing to maintain contemporaneous Local File and Master File, refusing to produce documentation upon CRA audit, or failing to file Country-by-Country Report where the group revenue threshold is exceeded
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Subsection 247(3) of the Income Tax Act imposes a transfer pricing penalty equal to 10% of the net adjustment where the taxpayer fails to make reasonable efforts to use arm's length pricing; documentation deficiencies trigger immediate penalty exposure; EIFEL rules deny excessive interest deductions; CbC non-filing attracts severe daily administrative monetary penalties and ongoing audit penalties; interest compounds on all reassessed balances
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing certifications or direct artificial intercompany pricing expose themselves to gross-negligence penalties and personal assessments for unpaid tax where section 160 applies to transferred assets; persistent cross-border price manipulation can support criminal tax evasion charges, economic sanctions, and director reprimands with travel restrictions
